references.text: The parallel passage in [ref:Matt 19:22|Matthew 19:22] tells the same event: the young man went away sad, for he had great wealth. Matthew adds that he was "young".
The parallel passage in [ref:Mark 10:22|Mark 10:22] describes the same scene where the man became sorrowful and walked away, because he possessed many possessions.

In [ref:Luk 18:24-25|Luke 18:24–25], Jesus comments on the man's reaction and says that it is easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God, which directly follows from the man's grief over being unable to let go of his wealth.

[ref:1 Tim 6:9-10|1 Timothy 6:9–10] warns that those who desire to be rich fall into temptation and traps, and that the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil. This illustrates why the rich man was sad—his wealth had taken hold of his heart.
[ref:Fork 5:9-10|Ecclesiastes 5:9–10] speaks about how whoever loves money never has enough. The man's sorrow reflects this attachment to wealth that prevented him from following Jesus.

In [ref:Luk 12:15|Luke 12:15], Jesus warns against greed and says that a person's life does not consist in the abundance of possessions. The rich man's sadness shows just how difficult it is to let go of material wealth.

[ref:Luk 8:14|Luke 8:14] describes in the parable of the sower that some are choked by riches and the cares of life so that they do not bear mature fruit. The rich man's reaction is a concrete example of this.
[ref:Sal 62:11|Psalm 62:10] admonishes: "When wealth increases, set not your heart on it." The rich man's sorrow shows that his heart was tied to his wealth rather than obedience to God.
In [ref:Matt 6:24|Matthew 6:24], Jesus says that no one can serve two masters—God and mammon. The rich man's sadness reveals that he could not choose God over his riches.

[ref:Hebr 12:15-17|Hebrews 12:15–17] uses Esau as an example of someone who sold his birthright for a single meal. Just as Esau traded blessing for something perishable, the rich man chose his possessions over eternal life.
